title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: dangerous-goods uplift on demurrage day rates
content:
## Scope

This rule of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category governs the uplift applied to demurrage day rates on the final demurrage line of a per-container record whose booking carries dangerous goods. It reads the cargo type of the booking.

## Rule

When the booking's cargo type is dangerous goods, every demurrage day rate is increased by the product's dangerous-goods uplift percentage of itself; otherwise no uplift applies.

## Equivalent statement

| Booking cargo type | Uplift on each demurrage day rate |
|---|---|
| dangerous goods | the product's dangerous-goods uplift percentage of that rate |
| any other cargo type | none |

## Worked example (hypothetical day rate of USD 100.00 and an illustrative uplift of 40 percent)

On a dangerous-goods booking, a demurrage day rate of USD 100.00 is increased by 40 percent of itself, that is by USD 40.00, and the day is billed at USD 140.00. On a booking of any other cargo type the same day is billed at USD 100.00.

## Points of judgement

**Q: Is the uplift a fixed amount per day?**
A: No. It is a percentage of each day's own demurrage rate, so it grows with the slab and the rate class of the day.
